aria: Animated recap of the 76ers' 111 to 104 home win over the Heat: Tyrese Maxey's step-back 3-pointer with 2:31 left that made it 111 to 95, quarter-by-quarter scoring, LeBron James' 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds, the top scorers, how the 76ers won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from StatMuse's game page for the 76ers' 111–104 home win over Miami on Nov 25, 2026, an NBA Cup group game: all 111 Philadelphia points and all 104 Miami points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (42 of 89, 14 of 35 from three, 13 of 17 FT for Philadelphia; 39 of 86, 8 of 31, 18 of 26 for Miami), rebounds (43–44), assists (29–24) and steals (9–4). The quarter scores (29–33–28–21 to 32–21–28–23) are also on the Covers matchup page; 62–53 at the half is in the AP, the Philadelphia Inquirer and Field Level Media, and 90–81 after three in Field Level Media. Points in the paint (44–60) are on StatMuse and Covers, bench points (25–20) on StatMuse and in the Miami Herald. The biggest leads (Philadelphia 16, Miami 8) are on StatMuse and Covers; Field Level Media also has 16. Player turnovers are not shown (StatMuse's player rows and team total differ by one). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

LeBron James had 25 points (a season high, Inquirer), 12 assists (a season high) and 10 rebounds: his first triple-double as a 76er and the 126th of his career, fifth all time (Inquirer; NBC Sports Philadelphia). In the second quarter he scored 14 straight Philadelphia points, turning a 36–33 deficit into a 47–39 lead (AP; Inquirer). Tyrese Maxey's 30 were his most since 38 against Charlotte on Oct. 31 (Inquirer). The loss ended Miami's seven-game winning streak (Miami Herald). Joel Embiid missed his second straight game with an illness, and Jaylen Brown was ruled out at halftime with left hamstring tightness (AP; Inquirer). Giannis Antetokounmpo returned from a one-game absence (groin) with 32 points and 14 rebounds (Miami Herald; Hot Hot Hoops). Miami closed on a 9–0 run after the 111–95 lead (Field Level Media). Next: Philadelphia visits Indiana and Miami visits New York, both Friday, both their last NBA Cup group game (AP; Covers).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Tyrese Maxey's 26-foot step-back 3-pointer with 2:31 left that made it 111–95: StatMuse's play-by-play has "T. Maxey makes 26' stepback three" (no assist) at 2:31 for 108–95 to 111–95; Field Level Media: "Maxey's three with 2:31 left made it 111-95," the largest lead; NBC Sports Philadelphia also describes the step-back three to 111–95 (it gives 2:29). So the board's 76ers +13 to +16 is 108–95 to 111–95. The defender and the spot on the floor are not described, so the step-back is drawn with the template's plain pull-up from about 26 feet. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Philadelphia 76ers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Maxey's listed 6-foot-2 and 200 pounds (Wikipedia), with arms scaled to the 6-foot-6 wingspan measured at the 2020 draft combine (Sportskeeda), in the 76ers' home white with No. 0 (Wikipedia) and his proposed look from kit/looks.json. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
